transcript.text: indesit oven stoped heating, fan goes round n light on but its stone cold after 20 mins. grill werks fine tho. any ideas b4 i call some1 out

Yes, I can certainly help with some ideas before you call anyone out. Since the fan runs and the grill works fine, we know the power is getting into the cooker, so this is usually down to either a simple setting issue or a failed heating element in the main oven cavity. The most likely causes are that it’s stuck on an automatic timer mode, set to a "fan only" defrost function, or that the fan-oven element itself has burned out. Please try these two safe checks first: make sure the clock is showing the correct time and not flashing (if it was off recently), and ensure you are using a standard baking symbol like a fan with a circle around it rather than just a fan icon. If those look right, switch to 180°C on that setting for ten minutes; if it stays stone cold while the grill works, the element is likely faulty.
clock is set n not flashing, its in manual. orange light comes on n stays on tho, never goes off. still no heat at 180 on the fan oven setting

Since you have confirmed the clock is set, manual mode is active, and 180°C on the fan setting still produces no heat while the grill works fine, this strongly suggests a failed fan-oven heating element or a fault in its power supply. The fact that the orange light stays on indicates the control thinks it should be heating, but the element isn't getting through to generate warmth. To help me find the correct replacement part for your specific Indesit model, could you please provide the model number? It is usually found on a label or sticker located on the frame around the oven door opening. If you cannot reach that label right now, we can certainly wait until you are able to get it.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its an Indesit IFW 6330 IX, read it off the plate on the door frame. also heard a little pop from inside the back last time it worked if thats any help

[Heading: Likely cause: fan oven element]
The little pop you heard from inside the back last time it worked, combined with the fact that the fan runs but there is no heat on the 180°C setting, strongly points to a failed fan oven element. Since the grill works fine and we have ruled out timer issues, the element itself is likely broken or has lost its connection at the terminals. You can find a matching replacement part for your Indesit IFW 6330 IX below; please double-check that the listing matches your model number before ordering to ensure it fits correctly. If you are not comfortable removing the back panel and testing the element with a multimeter, or if you prefer not to handle mains electricity yourself, then calling out an engineer is the better choice for safety and peace of mind.

ive no multimeter but i can isolate it at the cooker switch on the wall n take the back panel off. what shud i look for on the element b4 i order one?

[Heading: Likely cause: fan oven element]
Before you order, ensure the cooker is switched off at the wall and cool to touch, then remove the back panel to inspect the circular fan element. Look for any obvious signs of damage like blistering, cracks in the metal sheath, or burnt wiring where it connects to the terminals. If the element looks physically intact but still isn't heating, a multimeter would be needed to test for continuity, which you mentioned you don't have. Given your symptoms and the pop you heard earlier, this is almost certainly the part that has failed, so I recommend getting a replacement fan oven element for your Indesit IFW 6330 IX. You can find a matching part listed below; please check the description to ensure it fits your specific model before purchasing. If you are unsure about reassembling the cooker or feel uncomfortable with the electrical work, then calling out an engineer is the safer choice.

ok isolated it at the cooker switch n took the back panel off (4 screws). theres a blister/split in the coil near the bottom with a black mark on it. so is that the element dead then?

[Heading: Likely cause: fan oven element]
Yes, that blister and split in the coil with the black mark suggests the fan oven element has failed internally. Since you have already isolated the power at the wall switch and removed the back panel safely, you can be confident this is the cause of the no-heat issue while the grill still works fine. A matching replacement part for your Indesit IFW 6330 IX is shown below; please check the listing carefully to ensure it matches your model before ordering.
